taskTypes.label: Implement a feature
taskTypes.instruction: Design and implement the requested functionality end-to-end.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. Add a password-reset flow: user requests a reset by email, receives a single-use link valid for 30 minutes, and sets a new password. Must integrate with our existing UserService.
checklist: Where it fits in the existing code

taskTypes.label: Code / design review
taskTypes.instruction: Review the provided material critically. Identify issues, rank them by severity, and propose concrete fixes.
taskTypes.placeholder: Paste the code, PR diff or design to review, then say what kind of feedback you want (correctness, security, readability…).
checklist: What it is supposed to do

taskTypes.label: Debug an issue
taskTypes.instruction: Diagnose the root cause of the problem described. Form hypotheses, explain how to verify each, then propose a fix.
taskTypes.placeholder:
e.g. POST /orders returns 500 intermittently under load.
Error: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading "id") at OrderService.create (order.service.ts:42)
Expected: 201 with the order. Actual: 500 roughly 1 in 50 requests.

taskTypes.label: Refactor
taskTypes.instruction: Refactor the provided code to improve readability, structure and maintainability without changing its external behaviour.
taskTypes.placeholder: Paste the code to refactor and explain what bothers you about it (long functions, duplication, hard to test…).

taskTypes.label: System / solution design
taskTypes.instruction: Produce a solution design covering components, responsibilities, data flow, interfaces and key trade-offs.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. Design a notification service that sends email, SMS and push to 2M users per day, with user preferences, retries and delivery tracking.

taskTypes.label: API design
taskTypes.instruction: Design a clean, consistent, versionable API including endpoints/operations, request and response shapes, errors and auth.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. Design a REST API for managing subscriptions: create, upgrade/downgrade plans, cancel, and list invoices. Consumers are our web app and partners.

taskTypes.label: Optimise performance
taskTypes.instruction: Identify performance bottlenecks, explain their impact, and propose measurable optimisations in priority order.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. The /reports endpoint takes 4–6 s at p95. It runs 3 SQL queries over a 20M-row table. Target: under 500 ms.

taskTypes.label: Write tests
taskTypes.instruction: Write a thorough, maintainable test suite covering the happy path, edge cases and failure modes.
taskTypes.placeholder: Paste the code under test and say which framework to use and what level of tests you want (unit, integration, E2E).

taskTypes.label: Write documentation
taskTypes.instruction: Write clear, well-structured documentation tailored to the target audience.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. Write a README for our internal CLI that deploys preview environments. Readers are new engineers in their first week.

taskTypes.label: Explain a concept
taskTypes.instruction: Explain the concept clearly, building from fundamentals to practical application, with concrete examples.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. Explain how database isolation levels work and when to use each, with PostgreSQL examples.

taskTypes.label: Migration plan
taskTypes.instruction: Produce a safe, incremental migration plan with phases, risks, rollback strategy and validation steps.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. Migrate our monolith’s user module from MySQL 5.7 to PostgreSQL 16 with zero downtime. ~40 tables, 300 GB.

taskTypes.label: UI / UX design
taskTypes.instruction: Design the interface: layout, hierarchy, components, states and interactions, with rationale for each decision.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. Design the onboarding flow for a B2B analytics app: account setup, connecting a data source, and the first dashboard. Users are non-technical managers.

taskTypes.label: Compare options
taskTypes.instruction: Compare the candidate options objectively against relevant criteria and give a clear recommendation.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. Compare Kafka, RabbitMQ and AWS SQS for our order-event pipeline (~5k msg/s, ordering per customer, small team).

constraints.label: Production-ready
constraints.instruction: The solution must be production-ready, not a toy example.

constraints.label: Robust error handling
constraints.instruction: Handle errors and edge cases explicitly; never swallow errors silently.

constraints.label: Include tests
constraints.instruction: Include automated tests that cover the main behaviour and key edge cases.

constraints.label: Security best practices
constraints.instruction: Follow security best practices (input validation, least privilege, no secrets in code, OWASP guidance).

constraints.label: Performance-aware
constraints.instruction: Consider performance and scalability; call out time/space complexity where relevant.

constraints.label: Clean code / SOLID
constraints.instruction: Follow clean code and SOLID principles with clear naming and small, focused units.

constraints.label: Accessibility (WCAG AA)
constraints.instruction: Meet WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility requirements (contrast, keyboard access, semantics, focus states).

constraints.label: Minimal dependencies
constraints.instruction: Avoid introducing new third-party dependencies unless clearly justified.

constraints.label: Backward compatible
constraints.instruction: Preserve backward compatibility with existing interfaces and data.

constraints.label: Well commented
constraints.instruction: Comment non-obvious logic and document public interfaces.

constraints.label: Observability
constraints.instruction: Include structured logging, metrics and tracing hooks where appropriate.

constraints.label: Cost-conscious
constraints.instruction: Keep infrastructure and runtime cost in mind and call out cost implications.

reasoning.label: Ask clarifying questions first
reasoning.instruction: If any requirement is ambiguous or missing, ask concise clarifying questions before producing the final answer.

reasoning.label: State assumptions
reasoning.instruction: Explicitly list any assumptions you make.

reasoning.label: Think step by step
reasoning.instruction: Reason through the problem step by step before giving the final answer.

reasoning.label: Offer alternatives & trade-offs
reasoning.instruction: Present at least two viable approaches with their trade-offs, then recommend one and justify it.

reasoning.label: Self-review before answering
reasoning.instruction: Before finalising, review your answer against the requirements and success criteria and fix any gaps.

reasoning.label: Highlight risks
reasoning.instruction: Highlight risks, pitfalls and anything that needs human verification.

outputFormats.label: Structured Markdown
outputFormats.instruction: Respond in well-structured Markdown with clear headings, bullet points and fenced code blocks.

outputFormats.label: Code first, brief notes
outputFormats.instruction: Lead with complete, runnable code in fenced blocks, followed by brief explanatory notes.

outputFormats.label: Step-by-step guide
outputFormats.instruction: Respond as a numbered, step-by-step guide that the reader can follow in order.

outputFormats.label: Comparison table
outputFormats.instruction: Use a Markdown table to compare options, followed by a short recommendation.

outputFormats.label: Architecture Decision Record
outputFormats.instruction: Respond as an ADR with sections: Title, Status, Context, Decision, Alternatives Considered, Consequences.

outputFormats.label: Include diagrams (Mermaid)
outputFormats.instruction: Include Mermaid diagrams (in ```mermaid blocks) to illustrate architecture or flows.

outputFormats.label: JSON only
outputFormats.instruction: Respond with valid JSON only, no prose before or after it.

outputFormats.label: Checklist
outputFormats.instruction: Respond as an actionable checklist grouped by category.

audiences.label: Me (experienced engineer)
audiences.instruction: The reader is an experienced engineer: skip basics and be precise.

audiences.label: Junior developer
audiences.instruction: The reader is a junior developer: explain the reasoning and define jargon.

audiences.label: Engineering team
audiences.instruction: The reader is an engineering team: be precise and actionable.

audiences.label: Non-technical stakeholders
audiences.instruction: The reader is non-technical: avoid jargon and focus on impact, cost and risk.

tones.label: Concise
tones.instruction: Be concise and direct. No filler.

tones.label: Detailed
tones.instruction: Be thorough and detailed; completeness matters more than brevity.

tones.label: Mentoring
tones.instruction: Use a supportive, teaching tone and explain the why behind each recommendation.

tones.label: Formal
tones.instruction: Use a formal, professional tone suitable for documentation.

lengths.label: Short
lengths.instruction: Keep the response short (roughly under 300 words, excluding code).

lengths.label: Medium
lengths.instruction: Aim for a medium-length response (roughly 300–800 words, excluding code).

lengths.label: Long
lengths.instruction: A long, comprehensive response is welcome.

promptStyles.label: XML tags
promptStyles.hint: Best for Claude: clear section boundaries
